paper.title_en: Weak-field charged-scalar dynamics in Melvin--Kerr spacetime: an effective Kerr spectral problem
paper.abstract_en: We study the local weak-field reduction of the charged Klein--Gordon equation in the neutral-seed Melvin--Kerr geometry and the auxiliary Kerr spectral problem defined by that reduction. At fixed radius and fixed scalar charge, the metric has no term linear in the magnetic parameter $b$. In the chosen gauge the first-order Maxwell potential is $A_μ=b\,g_{μφ}$, so its interaction with an azimuthal mode $m$ is absorbed into $μ_{\rm eff}^{2}=μ^{2}+2qbm$. This identity applies to both separated equations and leaves the gauge-invariant horizon phase in the Kerr form. Extending the truncated equation to all exterior radii and imposing Kerr outgoing boundary conditions defines an auxiliary spectrum, evaluated with Dolan's continued-fraction method. Its linear magnetic response is the complex mass derivative of the Kerr spectrum. Numerical examples for the fundamental $\ell=1,2$ branches illustrate this relation, including the continuation through negative effective mass squared. The tabulated modes remain damped, and their real-frequency shifts have opposite signs for the two positive-frequency azimuthal sectors in the surveyed range. We separate numerical accuracy within the auxiliary problem from local weak-field power counting and the unresolved exterior boundary problem. No matching to the exact magnetized exterior is performed; consequently these frequencies are not established approximations to global Melvin--Kerr resonances.
